frontier.hypothesis: The trip-test cluster (target 127-130) and the blend arm's $v0/$v1 naming (target 122-123) are ONE sub-problem in the local allocator, not two: three source spellings of the trip test leave both unchanged, so the trip test should be treated as a dependent of the blend fix rather than attacked on its own.
frontier.mechanism: Both pseudos in the trip test are born and die inside the loop-bottom block, so they are local-alloc quantities (local-alloc.c), and the register left free for the first of them is decided by what the blend arm above is still holding in $v0/$v1. That is consistent with T1/T2/T3 all scoring 28 with identical 122/123 rows.
frontier.next_probe: Do not re-sweep the trip test. Instead dump .lreg/.greg for the W5 chassis (pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_8003DE14) and read which quantity holds $v0 across the blend arm's tail; then re-check the trip-test rows after ANY blend-arm change, as a free indicator of whether the blend fix is working.

frontier.hypothesis: The head residual (4 insns) is a reorg delay-slot exchange currently coupled to the seat, but the coupling may be breakable by removing `addiu a2,sp,1040` from reorg's candidate set WITHOUT moving `j = 0` back above the branch.
frontier.mechanism: reorg.c takes the closest movable insn before the branch. `dst = dst_buf` is that insn only because it is the last cursor initialisation emitted before the guard. If some other real statement the target also emits in 49-68 were scheduled last before the `blez`, reorg would take that instead and `addiu a2` would stay at 54 - though the slot then holds the wrong insn unless the chosen statement is itself dead on the taken path.
frontier.next_probe: H1 (dst before src), H3 (total last) and W11 (dst inside the guard) all failed at 28/30; the untried directions are (i) computing the outer-tail values in the outer do-body so a different insn is last before the guard, (ii) expressing the guard as `if (rect[2] * rect[3] > 0)` so the mult/mflo pair sits adjacent to the branch with nothing movable between, and (iii) reading the actual candidate list out of the .reorg / .jump2 dumps (pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_8003DE14) instead of inferring it.

frontier.hypothesis: The blend arm's residual (target 88-123) is now the only large cluster and is confirmed seat-independent, so it should be decided with tools/sched_solver rather than another source sweep.
frontier.mechanism: Twelve structurally distinct blend bodies score 28 or worse on the corrected-seat chassis, exactly as they scored 29 or worse on the s11 chassis - the difference is invariant under the source shape. sched.c:5106 both orders these insns and sets the live lengths feeding allocation, and the target runs the blue channel's srl/andi/mult before its first mflo (104-107) where we run it after (109-112).
frontier.next_probe: Dump the .sched RTL for the W5 chassis (bash tmp/grind/func_8003DE14/s12/dump.sh W5), feed the blend basic block to tools/sched_solver, and ask for the C-lever vectors that put the blue channel's mult ahead of the first mflo; classify with tools/ra_solver/inverse_compose.py classify before spending measurements, and gate each spelled form on build_insns == 173 and on the j/complement/dst seat rows being unchanged.
